title: Evaluation and first-order Taylor congruence for completed polynomial rings
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ a finitely generated ideal, $r\geq0$, and $P=\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_I$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For every commutative $A$-algebra $T$ complete for the ideal $IT$ and every tuple $y=(y_1,\ldots,y_r)\in T^r$, there is a unique continuous $A$-algebra homomorphism $E_y:P	o T$ with $E_y(x_i)=y_i$. Continuity is for the ideals generated by $I$. For each $i$, polynomial differentiation $\partial_i(x^
u)=
u_i x^{
u-\epsilon_i}$, with a zero term when $
u_i=0$, extends uniquely to a continuous $A$-linear map $\partial_i:P	o P$ satisfying the Leibniz rule. For every integer $s\geq1$, every tuple $z\in(I^sT)^r$, and every $f\in P$, one has
$$E_{y+z}(f)-E_y(f)\in I^sT,\qquad E_{y+z}(f)-E_y(f)-\sum_{i=1}^rE_y(\partial_i f)z_i\in I^{2s}T.$$
The coefficients $y_i$ are arbitrary elements of $T$, not required to lie in $IT$, and the assertions include $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation), with the quadratic error stated modulo I^(2s); evaluation is formal-spaces.tex Tag 0AJM (remark-universal-property). For noncomplete A this is the completion-of-polynomials formulation, constructed at each quotient A/I^m and then passed to the limit; no completeness of A is assumed.

proof.text: Put $S=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, $J=IS$, and let $\iota:S\to P$ be the completion map. If $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_t)$, then $J=(a_1,\ldots,a_t)S$ is finitely generated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] over the ring $S$, with ideal $J$ and module $S$. Thus $P$ is complete and separated and its component projection $\pi_n:P\to S/J^n$ has kernel $J^nP=I^nP$ for every $n\ge1$. Here $J^nP=I^nP$ because both are generated in $P$ by products of $n$ elements of $I$. Given $f\in P$, choose a polynomial $p_n\in S$ representing $\pi_n(f)$; then $f-\iota(p_n)\in I^nP$. This identifies the limit topology with the stipulated ideal-adic topology and supplies polynomial approximation without assuming $A$ complete or Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), parts (1),(2), applied to S and J

proof.text: For the prescribed tuple $y$, the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] gives $e_y:S\to T$. It sends $J^n$ into $I^nT$, since it fixes $A$, and hence induces $e_{y,n}:S/J^n\to T/I^nT$. Quotient reduction commutes with these maps: both composites send the class of a polynomial $p$ to the class of $e_y(p)$. Consequently $(e_{y,n}(\pi_n(f)))_{n\ge1}$ is a compatible family. By the bijection $T\simeq\varprojlim_nT/I^nT$ in [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], it determines a unique element $E_y(f)$. Componentwise addition, multiplication and constants show that $E_y$ is an $A$-algebra homomorphism; its value on $\iota(p)$ is $e_y(p)$, in particular $E_y(x_i)=y_i$.

source.place: Tag 0AJM (remark-universal-property), quotient-limit construction for completion of polynomials

proof.text: Every $A$-algebra map $u:P\to T$ sends $I^nP$ into $I^nT$: write an element of that ideal as a finite sum $\sum a_kb_k$ with $a_k\in I^n$ and use $u(a_kb_k)=a_ku(b_k)$. In particular $E_y$ is continuous. If $u(x_i)=y_i$, then $u\iota=e_y$ by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For the approximant $p_n$ of Step 1, both $u(f)$ and $E_y(f)$ reduce to $e_y(p_n)$ modulo $I^nT$. Their difference is in every $I^nT$, hence is zero by the injectivity in the completeness bijection of [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. This proves uniqueness, including among the continuous maps specified in the statement.

Let $d_i:S\to S$ be polynomial differentiation from [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. Since $d_i$ is $A$-linear, $d_i(\sum a_kp_k)=\sum a_kd_i(p_k)$ for $a_k\in I^n$, so $d_i(J^n)\subseteq J^n$. Thus it induces an $A$-linear $d_{i,n}:S/J^n\to S/J^n$; these commute with quotient reduction because both orders send $[p]$ to $[d_i(p)]$. Define $\partial_i f$ to be the compatible family $(d_{i,n}(\pi_n(f)))_n$ in the inverse-limit definition [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] of $P$. This is $A$-linear and extends $d_i$. If $f\in I^nP$, then $\pi_n(f)=0$ by Step 1, so $\pi_n(\partial_i f)=0$ and $\partial_i f\in I^nP$. In particular it is continuous.

source.place: Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation), meaning and construction of the continuous partial derivatives

proof.text: The polynomial Leibniz identity in [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] descends to each $S/J^n$: using representatives $p,q$, it is $d_{i,n}([p][q])=[p]d_{i,n}([q])+[q]d_{i,n}([p])$. Hence the two sides of the required identity for $f,g\in P$ have equal $\pi_n$ for every $n$, and are equal in the inverse limit [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For uniqueness let $D:P\to P$ be another continuous $A$-linear extension. $A$-linearity gives $D(I^nP)\subseteq I^nP$ by the same finite-sum argument as in Step 3. The approximant $p_n$ then gives $D(f)-\partial_i f\in I^nP$ for every $n$; separatedness from Step 1 forces equality.

source.place: Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation), derivative identities verified in polynomial quotients
Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation), explicit finite polynomial expansion supplying the omitted term-by-term calculation

proof.text: Choose the Step 1 polynomial $p=p_{2s}$ for $f$, so $f-\iota(p)\in I^{2s}P$. Step 3 gives $E_y(f)-e_y(p)$ and $E_{y+z}(f)-e_{y+z}(p)$ in $I^{2s}T$. Step 4 gives $\partial_i f-\iota(d_i p)\in I^{2s}P$, hence $E_y(\partial_i f)-e_y(d_i p)\in I^{2s}T$. Multiplying each of these last differences by $z_i$ stays in the ideal $I^{2s}T$. Therefore the quadratic remainder for $f$ differs from that for $p$ by an element of $I^{2s}T$, proving the second congruence by Step 6. The first difference similarly differs by an element of $I^{2s}T\subseteq I^sT$ from the first difference for $p$, proving the first congruence. If $r=0$, the sums are empty and there is only the empty tuple, so the two evaluation maps coincide and both differences are zero; the same constructions apply to $P=\widehat A_I$.

source.place: Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation), passage from polynomials to the completion modulo the fixed open ideal I^(2s)

There are no new nodes and no repair note. I read the source against Stacks restricted.tex Tag 0AK3 (remark-linear-approximation, l.862-881). The item is the case δ_i=z_i∈I^sT, so (z_iz_j)⊆I^{2s}T. It adds a first-order congruence mod I^sT and existence and uniqueness of the evaluation map. The evaluation follows 0AJM (formal-spaces l.6069), and noncomplete A is handled by 0AJN and 05GG. The statement keeps every hypothesis and is not weakened: I finitely generated, T complete for IT, arbitrary y, s≥1, r=0 included. Both of the parent's uses are covered (lem-per-power-split-uniform-adic-map-lifting: evaluation into C and C/K^m, and the Taylor congruence with z=-t). I read all four cited statements in full. Step 1 applies the leaf lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete (AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete/eval_surjective/pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval) to S=A[x], J=IS, M=S; J^nP=I^nP. Steps 2-3 build E_y from compatible quotient maps using completeness of T. Uniqueness follows from the polynomial universal property and separatedness of T; every A-algebra map is automatically continuous. Steps 4-5: the derivative preserves J^n by A-linearity, so it gives a continuous ∂_i with Leibniz at each level; uniqueness uses separatedness of P. Step 6 is the finite multinomial expansion: terms with exactly one z_i give e_y(d_i p)z_i, and terms with at least two z's lie in I^{2s}T. No factorials are divided. Step 7 approximates modulo I^{2s} and handles r=0. Every step checks, and each step marked elementary really is. I tested I=0, I=A, A=ℤ with T=ℤ_p and y a unit, and r=0. A duplicate search with rg -L for 0AK3, 0AJM, restricted, completed polynomial, Taylor and substitution found no duplicate. The proof cites only definitions and a Mathlib leaf, so there is no route, tool_uses or SGA issue.
